and never shells out, so it is engine-agnostic and podman changed nothing in it.

## Image updates — `internal/imageupdate` (§3.88)

## The OCI tables and the activity column — `internal/ui/oci_resources` (DEVDESK-146, A-09a; DEVDESK-153, A-09b)

The four tables of `:oci` (Images, Networks, Volumes, Registries) and the
registry browser's tag table are on the activity column (Rule 125; the router
side is in `app-shell.md`).

**Periodic refresh and terminal focus (DEVDESK-210).** `refreshInterval` is 10 s
(a var, so a test can shorten it). `RefreshTickMsg` used to refresh once and
never again; it now re-arms `tickCmd()` on every tick. While `Model.blurred` is
set (from `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`) the tick only re-arms and skips
`refreshReads()` (images, scan cache, networks, volumes; it never scans, Rule
126). On the focus edge (`Resume`) it runs `refreshReads()` once, with no new tick.

**Registry browser (DEVDESK-218, A-09a2).** The tag table
(`registry_browser.go`, built by `newTagTable`, which `ActivityTables` also uses
so the guard sees the real table open or not, as `oci/registry-browser`) takes
`datatable.IndicatorColumn` as column 0, an 8th column; Registry, Tag and
Updated are 1 to 3 (`tagColumnTag` = 2, `tagColumnUpdated` = 3). `tagRow` holds
`Activity components.RowActivity` and `ScanRunning`, stamped by
`rebuildTagTable` from `components.DescribeRow` (scan and pull, `ociKinds`,
target `jobs.TargetKey(imageName)`) over the snapshot the router pushes through
`SetJobs(runs, failures, context)`; the cell at rest is empty. While a scan
really runs (not queued) the C/H/M/L cells hold `…` in `DimStyle`; a queued scan
or a pull keeps the counts. The blink phase arrives with `SetBlinkPhase` and
`WantsBlink` is true for a visible running tag row. Rule 116: Updated drops
under 102 columns, L under 84, M under 78, H under 72, C under 66; at 60 only
the dot, Registry and Tag remain. The browser has no spinner of its own
(DEVDESK-374): a search shows the shared activity dot in the footer
(`Searching registries...`), and `WantsBlink` is true while it runs. After the search the
footer describes the selected tag (`Status{Detail}`). `tagScanSpinnerIdx` and
the local frame are deleted. `DescribeRow` filters by context: a scan of another
context no longer shows on a tag (D108).

**Networks, Volumes and Registries (DEVDESK-153, A-09b).** Each takes
`datatable.IndicatorColumn` as column 0. Rows carry no `components.RowActivity`:
the datatable reads its own busy marker (`MarkBusy`), and the column's
`Indicator` function returns `Idle` (or `Running` when `registryRow.refreshing`
is set). A remove, login or logout in flight is that marker, reported as
`Running` with its label (`BusyLabel`). On these three tables a failure never
leaves a `⊗` dot, only a footer message. On Registries, a group whose members are being discovered
(`refreshingGroups`) is `Running` too, and the Members cell is static dim text:
the row's dot says it, and `WantsBlink` is true while a group refreshes or a
row action runs, so the periodic refresh alone never blinks. The row spinner is
gone from the whole view: `advanceBusySpinners`, `busyTick`, `spinnerFrameIdx`
and every `AdvanceSpinner` call are deleted. The view's `spinner.Model` and `loadingRegs` are
deleted (DEVDESK-374): a tab's load, the tag search and the network inspection
show the shared activity dot in the footer (Rule 128), and `footerLoading()`
feeds `WantsBlink` with the same priority order as `formStatus()`. A load shows
only while the active tab's table is empty: `ctrl+r` on a filled table is
silent.

**Images (DEVDESK-146, A-09a).**

- **Column 0 is `datatable.IndicatorColumn`.** At rest it shows `IconDocker` in
  the `theme.IconRoleImage` role; while something runs it shows the state glyph.
  `imageRow.Activity` is stamped from `m.rowActivity` (`activity.go`), which
  calls `components.DescribeRow` on the router snapshot (`m.jobs`), the
  remembered failures (`m.failures`) and the snapshot's context.
- **The key is the raw reference, `jobs.TargetKey(img.Name())`.** There is no
  canonicalization: `nginx` and `docker.io/library/nginx` are two keys. Two
  images named `<none>` share one key, as they already share the scan cache
  entry. Kinds read are scan and pull, whoever started them.
- **Static words, no spinner frame in a cell.** The Scanned cell reads
  `scanning` and the ID cell reads `pulling` while the operation runs
  (`scanRunning`, `pullRunning`). The blink phase is read at render, so a frame
  rebuilds no row.
- **Removal is this view's own observation.** The busy `●`/`○` the table used to
  draw is gone; a removal in flight is reported as `Running` with its label
  (`BusyLabel`) and goes through the same column.
- **The footer describes the selected row** (`status()` in `view.go`), after the
  active tab's load state and beside the action line or the batch progress. A
  failed row's detail is fixed, so the spinner stays; a running or queued
  row's detail replaces it.
- **`failedScans` is removed.** A failure is read from `Failures` in the router
  snapshot and stays on the row until the next attempt.
- **After a successful removal the view calls `jobs.ForgetTarget(name)`**
  (`results.go`), so a deleted image does not keep a stale failure.

**Widths (Rule 116).** The activity column costs 4 cells (2 of width and 2 of
padding). Each optional column now appears 4 columns later (the before and after
thresholds, in terminal columns):

| Column | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Update | 48 | 52 |
| Secrets | 57 | 61 |
| C | 63 | 67 |
| H | 69 | 73 |
| M | 75 | 79 |
| L | 81 | 85 |
| Sig | 86 | 90 |
| Disk Usage | 100 | 104 |
| Content Size | 116 | 120 |
| Scanned | 132 | 136 |

At 60 columns the visible columns are `●`, ID, Name and Update. At 70 they are
`●`, ID, Name, Update, Secrets and C. At these widths the columns that give way
are required ones, which Rule 116 allows: a whole column goes, never a
truncated value.

A view in neither list, or an exempt view that is also migrated, fails by name (`classificationProblems`, unit-tested on fictitious classifications). A migrated view
exposes `ActivityTables() map[string]datatable.ActivityTable` (a read-only face:
**One rule for a busy row** (DEVDESK-137, DEVDESK-143): it shows `●` / `○` through
the `Indicator` column. A table with a `Key` but no `Indicator` column shows
nothing but greyed cells.

**Every table in the application is a `datatable`** (§3.21 moved the last four:
Registries, the registry browser's tags, network-inspect and netdiag's results).
A new table uses it; there is no second way to build one, and `bubbles/table` is
imported outside this package only for its `Styles` type.

The Registries tab is the one worth knowing about, because it shows **two
populations in one table** — the configured entries, and one group's discovered
members after `→`. `datatable.Model[T]` is generic over a single `T`, so
`registryRow` carries both and holds the index of the config entry it stands
for, `-1` for a member. That index is what `getSelectedRegistry` resolves
through: indexing `m.registries` by row number is right only while the table
neither sorts nor filters, which is exactly the dependency nothing signalled.
`explorerRow` exists for the same reason.

Three views keep a filter of their own, and deliberately. `security` selects
findings **by tab**, and `status` drives both its tables from one search box so
the header counts agree — in both cases the view filters and calls `SetItems`,
because a `FilterBar` query narrows a list that is already settled and these
decide which rows exist at all. `security` also calls `GotoTop` explicitly on a
tab change, which is the reset `SetItems` does not make. Its **severity** goes
the other way: four cumulative tokens the table owns, and its sort and its
search are the table's too. The
registry browser is the third: its text filter and its registry filter narrow
the tags *before* the table sees them, and its bar is drawn in the OCI view's
own footer rather than the table's. Its **sort** is the table's — `.` cycles
Tag and Updated through `CycleSort`, and `SetSort` is what puts a new search
back on the default order.

`status` is the two-table case: two `datatable.Model` plus a focus helper.
`Focus` and `Blur` carry the styles with them (Rule 118), so a tab switch does
not touch `SetStyles`.
  A *failed* one is not: an unreachable manager must not erase what was last
  known, which is why `registrymgr` distinguishes the two (D23).
- The `Members` column shows `count · TimeAgo(discovered_at)`, or `never`. It is
  not decoration: a cache with no visible age looks current whatever it holds.
- The **registry browser reads this cache**, never the network: it opens on the
  first frame and works offline. `→` on a group row in the Registries tab drills
  into its members, `←`/`esc` go back.
- `internal/cache/browser_selection.go` remembers what the browser had
  **un**checked, per context. Storing the exceptions is what makes a
  newly-discovered member arrive checked rather than silently excluded.
- **A picker entry is identified by `browserRegistryEntry.key`, never by its
  URL** (D40). Two registries may be declared on one host — the form enforces
  slug uniqueness, not URL uniqueness — so a URL ticks and unticks both, and the
  exclusion outlives the session. The key is the slug for a standalone registry
  and `memberKey(groupSlug, memberURL)` for a member; `Slug` alone will not do,
  since a member carries its *group's*. Read it through `selected(entry)` rather

Bearer. `Error()` keeps the three historical messages to the character
(`registry returned 404`, `token endpoint returned 403`,
`unexpected auth challenge: ...`), so nothing on screen or in a log changed.
Failures that are not a status (unreadable body, missing realm, no token
field) stay plain errors and do not match `errors.As`.

The unexported `unexpectedChallenge` field is a deviation from the plan, which
had only `Code`, `Source` and `Challenge`: with those three, a 401 with a
non-Bearer challenge and a 401 returned by the registry after a token exchange
both read `Source == SourceRegistry`, `Code == 401`, and `Error()` could not
give each its own message. The flag tells them apart without widening the
exported surface.

unchanged. A deadline or a cancel reaches the caller as an error that

input.message:
DEVDESK-397 est documentée, uniquement dans des fichiers Markdown du worktree feat-devdesk-299-image-search-level1. Aucun commit et aucun .go touché. Je n'ai pas relu les rendus ni lancé de lint Markdown.

**Fichiers modifiés** (chemins relatifs au worktree)
- `docs/architecture/network.md`
  - Section `internal/oci` : `oci.StatusError` (Code, Source, Challenge), messages inchangés au caractère près, et les échecs hors statut qui restent des erreurs simples. `unexpectedChallenge` est présenté comme un écart au plan, avec sa justification. Variantes `*Context` : échéance, annulation, vérification de `ctx.Err()` à chaque page. Limite notée : le client enveloppe aussi `DeadlineExceeded`, donc IS-12 ne pourra pas distinguer le timeout client de l'échéance du contexte.
  - Nouvelle section `internal/imagesearch` : Target, Query, Image, Searcher, SearcherFunc.
  - Section « OCI tables », avant « Networks, Volumes… » : génération globale `browserGen`, annulation par lot (`beginRequests`, `cancelInFlight`, seam `listRegistryTags`, `RegistryBrowserGen`).
  - Même emplacement : niveau 1 du browser (`browserStateImages`, aiguillage de `submitSearch`, `defaultImageSearcher` nil donc inactif jusqu'à IS-02, `imageSearchDeadline` 15 s par registre, `searchTable`, avertissement « No registry selected », erreur de recherche seulement journalisée jusqu'à IS-12).
- `docs/architecture/registries.md` : une puce sur la recherche d'images, qui lit les mêmes entrées, clés et identifiants (D40, D12, D39) et n'écrit pas la sélection.
- `docs/architecture/app-shell.md` : `oci/registry-search` ajouté à `migratedTables` (6 tables pour `:oci`). J'y ai aussi noté que le garde scanne `browser_flow.go` et `browser_images.go`.
- `docs/architecture/ui-components.md` : paragraphe sur le niveau 1.
  - Il utilise la barre de filtre du datatable (Rule 136).
  - `esc` ferme la barre, vide la requête confirmée, puis annule le lot et revient au formulaire, noté comme écart au plan.
  - `enter` ne fait rien.
  - Les raccourcis sont `/ Filter` et `esc Go back`, ou `enter/esc Close filter` pendant la saisie.
  - Le titre porte la saisie.
- `docs/backlog.md` : entrée **D129**, insérée avant D128 (les entrées sont classées de la plus récente à la plus ancienne ; D128 était le dernier numéro, D129 n'existait nulle part). Elle couvre : niveau 1 inactif en production jusqu'à IS-02 (options A/B/C du plan), `esc` qui annule le lot, génération globale, `unexpectedChallenge`, limite du timeout client contre l'échéance du contexte.
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` : la ligne de `network.md` dans le tableau d'architecture cite maintenant `internal/imagesearch`, `StatusError` et le niveau de recherche d'images.

**Points incertains**
- Je me suis appuyé sur le diff non commité tel quel (`handleImagesKeyMsg`, `GetShortcuts`, `GetHeaderInfo`, `browser_flow.go`). Si le coder change `view.go` ou `browser_images.go` en parallèle, à recouper : l'ordre de `esc`, les libellés des raccourcis, `imageSearchDeadline` passé en paramètre de `searchImagesCmd`.
- Dans D129, j'ai écrit « branche `feat-devdesk-299-image-search-level1` (uncommitted) » ; à ajuster avec le numéro de PR quand il existera. Le plan est cité comme non suivi.
- La section « Registry browser » de `network.md` ne décrit toujours pas le niveau 2 en détail ; je n'ai ajouté que ce que la tâche demandait.
- `docs-site` n'est pas touché, conformément au plan (rien de visible sous Q1-A).
